No.  

According to Meridian’s Business Travel Policy (travel.md), any **international trip** (or any trip whose total cost exceeds $2,000) **must be approved by a manager at Director level or above**. This requirement applies regardless of the traveler’s own seniority – even a Director would need a second Director‑or‑above approver for their own qualifying trip.

A Senior Manager is tier 3 in the seniority hierarchy (below Director), so they do **not** meet the “Director level or above” threshold. Therefore a Senior Manager cannot approve their own $2,500 international trip; the trip would need sign‑off from someone holding a Director, Vice President, or higher title.
